newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan construction loans fall for 21st month.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan construction loans fall for 21st month.

text.p: Loans extended by Taiwan banks to construction firms fell 9.99 percent to T$392.833 billion year on year in February, marking the 21st consecutive month of declines, the central bank said on Wednesday.

However, the bank noted in a statement that the pace of decline had slowed for the fifth consecutive month since the figure fell 20.66 percent year-on-year in September. This indicated a gradual bottoming-out of the property market, it said.
Loans to construction firms fell 13.53 percent in January.
Loans extended by Taiwan banks to all private businesses fell 2.48 percent to T$2.96 trillion in February from a year earlier, the bank added.
Banks have been particularly cautious in granting loans to firms in the construction sector, which has been in deep recession since the local property market peaked in 1989.
In August 1996, the central bank scrapped all selective credit controls on land to boost the property market and the economy, and analysts had expected the move to gradually take effect.

Taiwan's gross domestic product rose 6.62 percent year-on-year in the fourth quarter of 1996, up from 5.12 percent, 5.42 percent and 5.61 percent, respectively, in the first, second and third quarters of 1996.
